audience: Stem managers using Gross Profit Center
purpose: Explain how Gross Profit Center revenue, cost, billback, confidence, and exceptions relate so managers can trust drilldowns without confusing enrichment gaps for financial mismatches.

nodes.label: Gross Profit Center
nodes.manager_summary: A read-only operating proof that combines QuickBooks financial truth with Vinosmith enrichment to explain sales, credits, cost, billback, gross profit, and confidence.

nodes.label: QuickBooks Financial Truth
nodes.manager_summary: QuickBooks owns financial revenue, credit memos, transaction dates, customers, reps, quantities, and accounting tie-outs.

nodes.label: Vinosmith Enrichment
nodes.manager_summary: Vinosmith enriches QuickBooks lines with wine metadata, sold price label, price identity, and billback when the sold line is still present.

nodes.label: QuickBooks Header Net Sales
nodes.manager_summary: Invoice header subtotal less credit memo header subtotal for the selected date range.

nodes.label: QuickBooks Line Net Sales
nodes.manager_summary: Signed sum of invoice line amounts and credit memo line amounts for the selected date range.

nodes.label: Revenue Tie-Out
nodes.manager_summary: The app should show that header net sales and line net sales match before managers trust GP drilldowns.

nodes.label: Stable Extract Ordering
nodes.manager_summary: Large extracts must use stable unique ordering. Otherwise a page can duplicate some invoices and skip others while row counts still look plausible.

nodes.label: Gross Sales
nodes.manager_summary: Gross Profit Center revenue: signed QuickBooks line net sales, including credit memo reversals.

nodes.label: Credit Memo Reversal
nodes.manager_summary: Credit memo lines reverse revenue, quantity, billback, effective cost, and gross profit consistently.

nodes.label: Current QuickBooks Cost Estimate
nodes.manager_summary: Initial GP uses current QuickBooks item purchase cost as the cost basis and labels it explicitly as current item cost, not audited historical COGS.

nodes.label: Billback Earned
nodes.manager_summary: Billback is treated as earned economic recovery per bottle when matched from Vinosmith price data.

nodes.label: Effective Cost
nodes.manager_summary: Cost before billback minus earned billback recovery.

nodes.label: Confidence Bucket
nodes.manager_summary: Every line receives a bucket so managers can separate exact matches, lower-confidence enrichment, manual prices, samples, missing price enrichment, and credit-workflow artifacts.

nodes.label: Missing Vinosmith Price Enrichment
nodes.manager_summary: The QuickBooks line matched a Vinosmith sold line, but price/billback enrichment was unavailable. This is an enrichment issue, not a revenue mismatch.

nodes.label: Credit-Workflow Missing Vinosmith Line
nodes.manager_summary: Returns or credits may cause Vinosmith sold lines to be deleted or altered. QuickBooks remains the financial truth; this bucket explains the enrichment gap.

nodes.label: Samples / Zero-Dollar / 100% Discount
nodes.manager_summary: Free goods and samples are separated from normal GP so managers do not read them as bad commercial margin.

nodes.label: Manual Price, No Billback
nodes.manager_summary: Manual Vinosmith prices are admin-entered; the app should not apply Vinosmith billback and should flag the line.

nodes.label: Why Does Revenue Not Match?
nodes.manager_summary: First check the revenue tie-out and extract stability before assuming the business numbers are wrong.

manager_guidance: Start with the revenue tie-out: QuickBooks header net sales should equal Gross Profit Center line net sales for the same date range.
If a revenue extract does not match, verify stable unique pagination before concluding the business numbers are wrong.
Treat Vinosmith gaps as enrichment confidence issues unless QuickBooks revenue itself fails the tie-out.
Do not mix samples/free goods into normal commercial-margin interpretation.
Initial GP is operating/economic GP using current QuickBooks item cost and earned billback, not audited historical COGS.
